items.title: Short-frame, self-expanding, fully recapturable transcatheter aortic valve replacement device in pure aortic regurgitation: Procedural performance and 30-day outcomes.
items.abstract: Achieving stable anchoring and effective sealing remains the principal limitation of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) in patients with pure native aortic regurgitation (PNAR). A short-frame, fully recapturable self-expanding valve may expand the procedural margin by enabling iterative repositioning and implantation depth optimisation in non-calcified anatomy. We analysed 13 consecutive patients with symptomatic moderate-to-severe or severe PNAR who underwent transfemoral TAVR with the ScienCrown® (Lepu Medical, Beijing, China) system. The primary endpoint was technical success at exit from the procedure room according to VARC-3 criteria. Secondary endpoints included device success and early safety at 30 days. Technical success was achieved in all patients (13/13, 100%), and device success at 30 days was also achieved in all patients (13/13, 100%). The 30-day early safety endpoint was met in 12 patients (92.3%). The mean prosthesis size was 27.62 ± 1.26 mm, with a mean prosthesis diameter oversizing relative to the average annular diameter of 12.90 ± 3.54%; no balloon predilatation was performed. The mean number of deployment attempts was 1.62 ± 0.77. All procedures were completed without valve embolisation/migration, coronary obstruction, second-valve implantation, or emergency surgery. One patient (7.69%) developed complete atrioventricular block on postoperative day 3 and underwent permanent pacemaker implantation; no additional pacemaker implantations occurred through 30 days. Predischarge diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated no new acute cerebral infarction. At 30 days, there were no deaths, strokes or transient ischaemic attacks, myocardial infarction, life-threatening/major bleeding, major vascular complications, endocarditis, or valve-related reinterventions. Mean transvalvular gradients were 7.67 ± 5.20 mmHg, and all patients had improved or stable NYHA functional class with no moderate or severe residual aortic regurgitation. In this exploratory single-centre series, transfemoral TAVR using a short-frame, fully recapturable self-expanding valve achieved 100% technical success and favourable early safety and haemodynamic performance in selected patients with PNAR. Prospective multicentre studies with longer follow-up and appropriate comparator groups are warranted.

items.title: High-Frequency Low-Tidal Volume Ventilation and Procedural Efficiency in Atrial Fibrillation Catheter Ablation: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
items.abstract: To compare high-frequency low-tidal volume (HFLTV) ventilation with standard ventilation (SV) regarding procedural efficiency, airway mechanics, and clinical outcomes in atrial fibrillation (AF) catheter ablation. Retrospective, observational, nonrandomized cohort study. Electrophysiology laboratory of a single tertiary-care university hospital. There were 160 consecutive eligible adults undergoing first-time AF radiofrequency ablation under general anesthesia between June 2023 and May 2024. Patients received HFLTV (n = 80; respiratory rate 25-30 breaths/min, tidal volume 3-4 mL/kg, ETCO₂ maintained <50 mmHg) or SV (n = 80; tidal volume 6-8 mL/kg, respiratory rate 10-12 breaths/min) per attending anesthesiologist practice. All received propofol-remifentanil total intravenous anesthesia. Primary outcomes were total procedure time and radiofrequency ablation time; secondary outcomes were airway pressures, oxygenation, AF recurrence at 1 and 6 months, AF-related hospitalization, and complications. HFLTV was associated with lower median procedure time (110 v 128 minutes; p < .001) and ablation time (23 v 28 minutes; p < .001). Peak (14 v 18 cmH₂O) and minimum (13 v 15 cmH₂O) airway pressures were lower with HFLTV (both p < .001), whereas ETCO₂ and SpO₂ nadir were comparable. Multivariable regression identified HFLTV as an independent predictor of shorter ablation time (nonstandardized β=-5.48 minutes; 95% CI -7.05 to -3.91; p < .001). In exploratory analyses, recurrence at 1 month (7.5% v 15.0%; p = .211) and 6 months (13.8% v 18.8%; p = .520) and 6-month AF-related hospitalization (12.5% v 18.8%; p = .384) were numerically lower with HFLTV but confidence intervals were wide and included no difference. In a consecutive cohort including paroxysmal and persistent AF, HFLTV was associated with shorter procedure and ablation times and lower measured airway pressures without compromising gas exchange. Clinical outcome analyses were exploratory and hypothesis-generating, warranting prospective randomized evaluation.

items.title: Radio-Biological Enhancement of an Interleukin-6 Receptor Antibody by the β-Particle-Emitting Radionuclide Iodine-131 in Multiple Myeloma.
items.abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) is a hematologic malignancy defined by the accumulation of neoplastic plasma cells in the bone marrow. Although novel therapies have improved outcomes in patients with MM, most cases eventually relapse and become refractory, highlighting the need for new therapeutic strategies. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) plays a key role in MM progression by promoting tumor cell growth and survival. It promotes the growth of IL-6-dependent MM cells, and inhibition of IL-6 signaling could suppress their proliferation. However, the efficacy of the anti-IL-6 receptor antibody (Ab) tocilizumab (Toc) appears to be limited in IL-6-independent cases, and its clinical application has not yet been established. To enhance the therapeutic efficacy of Toc, an iodine-131 ( 131 I)-labeled Toc was evaluated as a β-emitting radioimmunotherapy (RIT), which combines Ab specificity with the cytotoxicity of radionuclides to deliver targeted radiation to MM cells. In vitro assays demonstrated that the 131 I-labeled Toc induced growth inhibition in both IL-6-responsive and IL-6-irresponsive MM cells. Furthermore, biodistribution studies and therapeutic evaluation in an MM xenograft mouse model revealed selective tumor accumulation and significant tumor growth suppression following intraperitoneal administration. These findings suggest that 131 I labeling enhances the antitumor activity of Toc and may overcome the limitations of Toc monotherapy. Therefore, β-emitting RIT using 131 I represents a promising strategy for MM, and further investigation into its mechanistic details is warranted.

items.title: Cerebral Attack With Cortical-Leptomeningeal Involvement and Seizures in AQP4-IgG-Positive Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder.
items.abstract: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) rarely presents with corticalleptomeningeal involvement. A 47-year-old woman with aquaporin-4 immunoglobulin G (AQP4-IgG)-positive NMOSD developed acute headache, seizures, motor aphasia, and worsening right arm weakness. Brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed a tumefactive-appearing left frontal cortical-subcortical lesion with leptomeningeal enhancement. The clinical and radiological abnormalities improved after immunotherapy. This case illustrates a rare cerebral manifestation of AQP4-IgG-positive NMOSD with cortical-leptomeningeal involvement, seizures, and a tumefactive lesion.

items.title: Plasma cell-free RNA ITGB3 is associated with long-term clinical benefit in patients with non-small cell lung cancer receiving immunochemotherapy.
Zinc peroxide-coated gold nanorods as the therapeutic adjuvants for photothermal enhanced chemodynamic therapy and metalloimmunotherapy against tumor.
items.abstract: Traditional tumor therapies have limited efficacy, leading to a high mortality rate. Although immunotherapy holds considerable therapeutic promise, clinical immunotherapy for solid tumors only elicits durable responses in a minority of patients. This limitation is largely attributed to the highly immunosuppressive nature of the tumor microenvironment (TME). Notably, conventional chemodynamic therapy (CDT) is hampered by endogenous hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) shortage in tumor cells, and AZP compensates this defect via in-situ H 2 O 2 self-supplementation to amplify hydroxyl radical generation. To develop a nanoplatform capable of systematically enhancing anti-tumor immunity, we rationally constructed a PEGylated zinc peroxide-coated gold nanorod (AZP) as a therapeutic adjuvant with acid-responsive properties for the combination therapy of cancer. Gold nanorod-based adjuvants coated with zinc peroxide were successfully prepared via chemical oxidation, followed by PEGylation. The morphology and size of the AZP were characterized using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and hydrodynamic diameter measurements. The elemental composition of AZP was determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis. The acid-responsive degradation and photothermally enhanced catalytic properties of AZP were evaluated using TEM, inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry, absorption spectroscopy, and thermal imaging tracing. The therapeutic mechanism of AZP at the cellular level was investigated through a series of experiments, including TEM, fluorescence imaging, immunofluorescence assays, Seahorse analysis, western blotting, and bioinformatics approaches, which comprehensively clarified the anti-tumor mechanism of AZP. Bilateral tumor and metastatic tumor models were established to verify the anti-tumor efficacy and mechanism of AZP at the animal level. Specifically, fluorescence imaging, immunofluorescence staining, tissue staining analysis, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and flow cytometry were performed to assess the in vivo therapeutic effects. In the acidic TME, the AZP nanoplatform releases H 2 O 2 and zinc ions, which increases the reactive oxygen species level in cancer cells. Additionally, due to its photothermally enhanced peroxidase-like activity, AZP induces the generation of more hydroxyl radicals under light irradiation. These effects synergistically disrupt lysosomes and mitochondria in tumor cells, block autophagy, and ultimately lead to tumor cell death. Furthermore, zinc supplementation by AZP enhances the activation of the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase and stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway. Meanwhile, the combined treatment induces immunogenic cell death of cancer cells, which promotes the release of tumor-associated antigens and activates robust anti-tumor immune responses. Notably, intratumoral injection of the AZP adjuvant combined with irradiation effectively eradicates in situ tumors. When further combined with PD-1 antibody, this regimen can induce anti-tumor immunity, significantly inhibiting tumor growth, metastasis, and recurrence in a murine model without causing obvious toxicity. The AZP nanoplatform exhibits excellent therapeutic efficacy, providing a rational design strategy for a potent adjuvant that integrates photothermally enhanced chemodynamic therapy and metalloimmunotherapy for the treatment of solid tumors.

items.title: A self-amplifying IL-1β-CCL2 circuit between macrophages and cancer-associated fibroblasts drives colorectal cancer progression.
items.abstract: Reciprocal interactions between immune and stromal cells are increasingly recognized as major determinants of colorectal cancer (CRC) progression. However, the specific macrophage and fibroblast states cooperating to establish and sustain a tumor-promoting microenvironment remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify a self-reinforcing inflammatory circuit linking monocyte-derived IL-1β + macrophages with IL1R1 + cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) in CRC. Integrated single-cell transcriptomic analyses of human CRC revealed a marked expansion of IL1B-associated inflammatory macrophages and IL1R1 + inflammatory CAFs, with their respective and combined transcriptional signatures associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Pseudotime analysis and Ms4a3 lineage tracing supported a predominantly monocyte-derived origin of IL-1β + macrophages in the tumor microenvironment. Mechanistically, macrophage-derived IL-1β activated IL1R1 signaling in fibroblasts, promoting the acquisition and expansion of an inflammatory CAF state. Myeloid Il1b deletion or fibroblast-lineage Il1r1 deletion disrupted this interaction and suppressed tumor growth in vivo. In turn, IL1R1 + CAFs produced abundant CCL2, which recruited CCR2 + monocytes and replenished the IL-1β + macrophage population. Fibroblast-lineage Ccl2 deletion, myeloid Ccr2 deletion, and CCL2 rescue experiments established the functional requirement of the CCL2-CCR2 axis for closure of this reciprocal circuit. Acquisition of the IL-1β + inflammatory macrophage program was further supported by coordinated NF-κB and AP-1 activity, with RELA and JUN/FOS contributing to IL1B transcriptional regulation. Finally, therapeutic blockade of either IL-1β or CCL2 disrupted the macrophage-CAF circuit, increased intratumoral CD8 + T-cell responses, and enhanced the antitumor efficacy of anti-PD-1 therapy. Collectively, our findings establish the IL-1β-IL1R1-CCL2-CCR2 axis as a self-amplifying immune-stromal circuit that sustains a tumor-promoting and immunosuppressive microenvironment in CRC. By demonstrating that disruption of this circuit restores antitumor immune activity and sensitizes tumors to PD-1 blockade, our study provides a mechanistic and preclinical rationale for targeting IL-1β-CCL2-mediated macrophage-CAF crosstalk as a combination strategy to improve immunotherapy responses in CRC.

items.title: Accelerated Systemic Atherosclerosis Following Immune-Related Adverse Events in a Patient with Primary Thoracic Melanoma: A Case of Sequential Coronary and Peripheral Revascularization.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) improve survival in advanced melanoma, but they may accelerate atherosclerosis, particularly in patients with immune-related adverse events (irAEs). A 64-year-old man with stage IV BRAF-wild-type primary thoracic melanoma achieved complete remission after nivolumab plus ipilimumab, but he later developed grade 3 immune-related hepatitis, requiring treatment discontinuation. Three and a half years later, symptomatic peripheral artery disease required revascularization, followed by severe coronary artery disease requiring percutaneous coronary intervention one year later. This case suggests that severe irAEs may be associated with accelerated systemic atherosclerosis, highlighting the importance of long-term cardiovascular surveillance following ICI therapy.

items.title: Genetic Modulation of ALT Leads to Underestimation of Liver Injury in Male ALDH2*2 Drinkers.
items.abstract: Serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) is commonly used to detect hepatocellular injury. However, genetic and metabolic factors may modulate ALT levels. We focused on the potential impact of an in-activating mutation in aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2*2, rs671) polymorphism, prevalent among East Asians, on ALT levels and its interaction with alcohol consumption. We analyzed Taiwan's Biobank data of 91,743 participants, 48.7% of whom were ALDH2*2 carriers, to assess the interaction between ALDH2 genotype, alcohol consumption and serum levels of liver enzymes. Mechanistic studies were conducted using ALDH2*2 knock-in (KI) mice exposed once to ethanol (1 g/kg), to evaluate ALT expression and serum levels, inflammation and liver injury. Integrative transcriptomic analyses, along with validation using publicly available datasets, were performed to identify transcriptional regulators of ALT. Male ALDH2*1/*2 drinkers exhibited a significantly lower serum ALT levels compared to ALDH2*1/*1 drinkers, despite higher gamma-glutamyl transferase levels (p < 0.001). Following acute ethanol administration to ALDH2*1/*2 mice, serum ALT elevation remained minimal despite comparable or greater accumulation of lipid oxidation product, 4-hydroxynonenal, enhanced MAPK activation, increased chemokine expression, and markedly aggravated histological necrosis relative to ethanol-treated wildtype mice. Notably, hepatic Alt1 mRNA and ALT protein expression were significantly reduced in ethanol-treated ALDH2*1/*2 mice. Integrated ChIP-seq analysis suggested that the transcription factor Hnf4a/HNF4A may regulate Alt1/ALT1 transcription. Validation using publicly available datasets confirmed reduced hepatic ALT1 expression in early inflammatory states and in patients with alcoholic hepatitis. ALDH2 deficiency blunts serum ALT elevation following alcohol exposure by limiting hepatic ALT expression. These findings underscore the importance of considering ALDH2 genotype when interpreting serum ALT levels in male drinkers and provide a rationale for further investigation of genotype-informed ALT interpretation in East Asian populations. We found that serum ALT levels may underestimate liver injury in alcohol-consuming individuals carrying the ALDH2*2 (inactive) allele; genetic background and environmental factors may be considered when interpreting liver injury based on serum ALT, a commonly used clinical biomarker. Since previous studies have shown that ALDH2*2 carriers are at increased risk of alcohol-related liver disease, incorporating genotype-informed clinical strategies may improve early detection and clinical outcomes. These findings are particularly important for East Asian populations, where ALDH2*2 is common. None.

items.title: Spleen stiffness to rule out high-risk varices in advanced chronic liver disease: an individual patient data meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Management of esophageal varices (EV) is of critical importance in compensated advanced chronic liver disease. We conducted an individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis to (i) investigate the performance of spleen stiffness measurement (SSM)-based algorithms using vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) to rule out high-risk varices (HRV); (ii) develop a new model for diagnosing any grade EV. We systematically searched databases for studies reporting endoscopy and SSM-VCTE data in adult patients, collecting their IPD. The main outcome was ruling out HRV. The tested algorithms were: i) Baveno-VI criteria, liver stiffness measurement (LSM) 150x10 9 /L); ii) SSM ≤40 kPa; iii) combined Baveno-SSM criteria ≤40 kPa in patients outside Baveno VI criteria. We developed and internally validated logistic regression models to diagnose any grade EV. Twenty studies comprising 2257 patients were included, with a summary HRV prevalence of 25%. The Baveno VI algorithm showed 100% (95%-CI:97-100%) sensitivity and 100% (95%-CI:95-100%) NPV; the rate of spared endoscopies was 17% (95%-CI:15-18%). The combined Baveno VI-SSM criteria performed best for ruling out HRV: 97% (95%-CI:94-99%) sensitivity, 98% (95%-CI:96-99%) NPV and rate of spared endoscopies of 35% (95%-CI: 34-38%). These results were robust in all sensitivity analyses, including patients with non-viral etiology (n=637) and studies using the 100 Hz module. We developed new logistic models with excellent accuracy for the diagnosis of EV, but the ability to identify patients at low risk (<10%) of EV was limited. This large, multicenter, international study validated spleen stiffness measurement as an accurate tool to assess high-risk esophageal varices. The combined Baveno-SSM algorithm performed best in ruling out HRV. Spleen stiffness has been recommended to rule out high-risk varices, but the evidence supporting its use is of low-quality. Our individual patient data meta-analysis, which included more than 2200 patients with compensated cirrhosis, showed that spleen stiffness ≤40 kPa can rule out high-risk varices with a very low rate of false negatives. Its combination with Baveno VI criteria was the most efficient triage strategy, doubling the rate of endoscopies that could be safely avoided compared to using the Baveno VI criteria alone. The findings of our study strengthen the level of evidence supporting the use of spleen stiffness as an additional screening tool for high-risk varices.

items.title: Meeting Report: 39th International Conference on Antiviral Research in Prague, Czech Republic, April 27-May 1, 2026.
items.abstract: The 39 th International Conference on Antiviral Research (ICAR), hosted by the International Society for Antiviral Research (ISAR), took place April 27-May 1, 2026, at the Cubex Centrum Praha in Prague, Czech Republic. The annual meeting brought together scientists from academia, industry, government, and public health to present recent advances across antiviral discovery, therapeutic development, vaccine research, host-directed approaches, and preparedness for emerging and re-emerging viral threats. The 2026 program included plenary and award lectures, oral presentations, poster sessions, late-breaking presentations, shotgun presentations, and focused scientific sessions spanning arboviruses, coronaviruses, influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), chronic, latent, and persistent viruses, hepatotropic and gastrointestinal viruses, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven drug discovery, broad-spectrum antiviral drugs, non-respiratory biothreat viruses, and pandemic preparedness. The opening plenary featured lectures on influenza virus and hepatitis D virus entry inhibition, while ISAR award lectures highlighted major contributions to antiviral science, including global virus research, antiviral and vaccine development, broad-spectrum antiviral approaches, rational drug design, and small-molecule development for yellow fever disease. ICAR 2026 also included dedicated activities to support professional development and community building, including the Women in Science Roundtable, First Timer and New Member Morning Coffee, PechaKucha Competition, the Chu Family Foundation Fellowship presentations, ISAR Annual Meeting, and Career Development Interactive Roundtable. Overall, ICAR 2026 reinforced ISAR's role as an international forum for scientific exchange, interdisciplinary collaboration, and development of the next generation of antiviral researchers.

items.title: Circulation and recombination-driven diversity of duck hepatitis B virus in domesticated geese in Guangdong, southern China.
items.abstract: Duck hepatitis B virus (DHBV) is a valuable comparative model for human hepatitis B virus (HBV) due to its shared genomic organization and reverse transcription-based replication, despite having only ∼40% nucleotide identity. Infection is generally asymptomatic in adult birds but causes reduced hatchability, impaired embryo development, and growth retardation in young waterfowl, leading to economic losses. As a major waterfowl producer, China faces risks from this endemic virus. This study analyzed 901 deceased domesticated geese liver samples from five regions in Guangdong province, southern China. Nested PCR screening revealed an overall infection prevalence of 34.1% (307/901). Amino acid analysis of the preS domain of the large envelope protein showed extensive variability, including the G133E mutation in 47.7% (21/44) of strains and genotype-associated substitutions at residues 117 and 120. Genetic characterization of 44 complete genomes revealed exclusive circulation of genotypes I and II (DHBV-I and DHBV-II), with no detection of the Western-associated DHBV-III. Phylogenetic analysis indicated frequent duck-goose host-switching and viral circulation between provinces, likely facilitated by the live-poultry trade. We identified 20 recombination events, six of which involved our sequences as parental strains, demonstrating that active recombination among co-circulating strains drives viral heterogeneity in Guangdong. These findings highlight the ongoing circulation and evolutionary complexity of DHBV in southern China and underscore the need for longitudinal genomic surveillance to detect emerging variants.

items.title: Sequential Liver, Kidney, and Heart Transplantation in a Single Recipient: Long-Term Survival Complicated by Chronic Renal Allograft Failure, Lung Cancer, and Recurrent Infection-A Case Report.
items.abstract: Multi-organ transplant recipients face a substantial long-term risk of infection, malignancy, and chronic rejection secondary to prolonged immunosuppression. Sequential liver, kidney, and heart transplantations remain rare, resulting in limited evidence to guide perioperative management and long-term follow-up. A 61-year-old man underwent sequential liver, kidney, and heart transplantations in 2012, 2018, and 2022, respectively. Initial graft function was favorable under an immunosuppressive regimen comprising tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and corticosteroids. From 2023 onwards, he developed recurrent SARS-CoV-2 infections, lung cancer requiring a segmentectomy, recurrent lower-extremity arteriosclerosis obliterans, and progressive renal allograft failure. He ultimately died from cardiopulmonary arrest precipitated by severe metabolic acidosis and electrolyte derangements complicating renal allograft failure. This case suggests that patients undergoing sequential multi-organ transplantations can achieve meaningful long-term survival with multidisciplinary care and individualized immunosuppression. Nevertheless, complications related to cumulative immunosuppression remain a major challenge, necessitating dynamic follow-up and tailored post-transplant management. Sequential liver, kidney, and heart transplantations are feasible in carefully selected patients. However, the delayed adverse effects of chronic immunosuppression pose a major threat to long-term outcomes, underscoring the absolute necessity for vigilant monitoring and highly individualized pharmacological management.

items.title: Socioeconomic inequalities in treatment for colorectal liver metastases in England: A competing risk analysis using National Cancer Registration Dataset.
items.abstract: There has been a wide variation, as well as socioeconomic inequalities, in liver resection rate for people diagnosed with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) in England. Currently, service specification in England requires providers to follow locally agreed referral pathways. However, decisions about patient referral to specialist multi-disciplinary teams (MDTs) may depend on local primary site-specific MDTs. We aimed to assess socioeconomic inequalities in the probability of undergoing liver resection/ablation (liver treatment), among patients diagnosed with synchronous/metachronous liver metastases (sLM/mLM). We identified patients diagnosed with colorectal cancer from 2015 to 2022 using the National Cancer Registration Dataset, and those with CRLM using the administrative dataset. We conducted a competing-risk analysis using flexible parametric regression models to estimate liver treatment-specific hazard up to one year after CRLM diagnosis by SES. We also derived cumulative probabilities of receiving treatment (CPr Ltx ), handling death as the competing event. The population-level CPr Ltx was 8.7% (95% confidence interval [CI] 8.5 to 9.0%) for sLM (36 660 patients) and 23.5% (95% CI 23.1 to 24.0%) for mLM (25 159 patients). The adjusted CPr Ltx gap between the least and most deprived groups reached 2.6% (1.8 to 3.5%) for sLM and 1.0% (95% CI -0.2 to 2.3%) for mLM. Socioeconomic inequalities in liver treatment receipt persisted for sLM. Referral of all patients with CRLM to hepato-pancreato-biliary (HPB) specialists is recommended, irrespective of SES of patients. Potential policy lever could be promoting proactive HPB specialist involvement in local colorectal multi-disciplinary meetings to reduce variation in referral. (250 words).

items.title: Genetic hepatocellular cholestasis: an update.
items.abstract: Cholestasis, defined as a reduction of bile flow, may be secondary to obstruction of bile ducts or absence of production of bile by hepatocytes. Genetic hepatocellular cholestasis is a heterogenous group of diseases, including bile acid synthesis defects (BASD) and progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis (PFIC). It affects a gene involved in either bile acid synthesis (BASD) or bile secretion by hepatocytes (PFIC). Recent advances in molecular biology and sequencing techniques have enabled the identification of many novel cholestatic disorders beyond the three historical PFIC. These diseases, of variable severity, are responsible for chronic cholestasis, intractable pruritus and often progress toward early liver cirrhosis, liver failure and liver cancer. Novel therapeutics such as ileal bile acid transporter inhibitors have been developed for the treatment of pruritus. Many patients with genetic hepatocellular cholestasis will require liver transplantation during childhood because of intractable pruritus or worsening of liver function. Specific subsets of BASD manifesting as chronic cholestasis are treatable with primary bile acid therapy with excellent native liver survival in the long-term. In this publication, we will review the clinical, biochemical and molecular features of genetic hepatocellular cholestasis, as well as their management.

When to Operate After Neoadjuvant Therapy for Borderline Resectable Pancreatic Cancer: A Critical Review and Multidimensional Decision Framework.
items.abstract: Surgical timing after neoadjuvant therapy for borderline resectable pancreatic cancer remains difficult because post-treatment imaging may not reliably distinguish residual tumor from fibrosis, whereas tumor biology and patient fitness strongly influence surgical benefit. We performed a critical narrative review of studies and guidelines addressing surgical timing, radiological response, tumor-marker dynamics, pathological response, and physiological readiness after neoadjuvant therapy for borderline resectable pancreatic cancer. Current evidence supports a multidimensional approach rather than reliance on anatomical imaging alone. Informative tumor-marker trajectories, especially carbohydrate antigen 19-9 when reliable and alternative markers such as Duke pancreatic monoclonal antigen type 2 when carbohydrate antigen 19-9 is non-informative, are central to assessing systemic disease control. Selective use of liver magnetic resonance imaging, diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging, and positron emission tomography-based modalities may help clarify discordant scenarios or detect occult metastatic disease. Patient fitness, including performance status, nutritional reserve, organ function, and recovery from treatment-related toxicity, remains essential before exploration. Surgical timing after neoadjuvant therapy for borderline resectable pancreatic cancer should integrate biology, anatomy, and patient condition. A biology-first multidisciplinary framework may help avoid futile pancreatectomy while preserving timely surgical opportunities for appropriate candidates.
